package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package or code is described in this report. The article discusses general supply chain security threats and the Pyrsia project's approach to mitigating them, but does not provide any concrete examples of malicious code or packages.

behavioral_signatures: Modification of code after source control (unauthorized changes post-commit)
Builds performed on compromised or untrusted platforms
Use of dependencies from untrusted or compromised sources
Bypassing CI/CD pipelines or code review processes
Distribution of packages from compromised repositories
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in build artifacts not matching source control
Presence of dependencies not declared in official manifests
Build scripts or CI/CD configurations altered outside of normal workflow
network_indicators: Connections to untrusted or unexpected package repositories
Unexpected network activity during build or install phases
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized changes to source code after it leaves source control, validate build integrity by comparing build outputs to source, enforce strict dependency provenance, and audit CI/CD and package repository access for anomalies. Use tools that verify package signatures and provenance, and alert on deviations from expected workflows.
